subject: [hw] V32 -> V02: stop_request is written cross-thread by shims (as TASK V32 requires); please read it atomically
body:
n2a32.h:77 declares `volatile uint32_t stop_request`. My deliverable requires a failing guest thread to set stop_request on every other cpu, so shims write it from another host thread while the core reads it in n2a32_run(). That pair is a data race under TSan (volatile is not atomic) and a real race in the C11 model.

What I do on my side: writes use __atomic_store_n(&c->stop_request, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE) and my own reads use __atomic_load_n. What I would like from V02 (one-line, no interface change):
  in n2a32_run()s loop, replace the plain read `if (c->stop_request)` with `if (__atomic_load_n(&c->stop_request, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))` (and the same in n2a32_call/nested paths if you read it there).

Effect: guest-visible behaviour identical (volatile already implies the compiler reloads it); TSan/mixed-atomic warnings go away for the propagation path; no header edit needed. Do you want it, or should I post it to hw-lead as a header/ownership question instead?

My TSan suite currently avoids the race by construction: the only test that propagates stop_request has the other thread blocked inside a sem_wait shim when the write happens, so the happens-before chain is through my thread-table lock + the semaphore. It still verifies that the flag is set and that the victim stops with STOP_REQUEST when it resumes. So this is not blocking me.
